prompt: What does a solid yellow center line mean?

decisions.prompt: What does a solid yellow center line mean?

options.consequence: You thought the solid line allowed passing and pulled out to pass the truck. A car came over the hill in the lane you pulled into and had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.

A center line does mark two-way traffic, but a solid line on your side also means no passing. You pulled out to pass anyway. A car came over the hill in the lane you pulled into and had to swerve onto the shoulder to miss you.
You thought your lane was ending and moved right. There is no lane there, only the shoulder and a guardrail, and you had to brake hard.

successText: You waited. A car came over the hill in the lane you would have been in. Once the line was broken again, you passed with a clear view.
ruleText: A solid yellow center line on your side means no passing; double solid yellow lines mean no passing in either direction.

citation.source: FHWA Manual on Uniform Traffic Control Devices, 11th Edition

verified: Read in the FHWA PDFs, Nov 2026: the sign "shall be installed on the left-hand side of the roadway at the beginning of no-passing zones"; passing "is prohibited for traffic traveling adjacent to the solid line".
